taxonomy.kew_note: Kew accepts this Texas endemic species.

project_inclusion.regional_note: Native to south-central Texas. Historical herbarium material includes a specimen collected about 6.3 miles northeast of San Marcos.

morphology_keys.habit: Widely branching spiny herb to roughly 0.8 m; stems prickly throughout.
morphology_keys.foliage: Leaves deeply lobed; lower surface sparingly to copiously prickly on and sometimes between veins; upper surface less prickly.
morphology_keys.flower: Large white flower, roughly 8–12 cm broad; numerous stamens.
morphology_keys.bud_sepals: Bud body about 18–25 × 14–18 mm; sepal horns angular or flattened, about 8–12 mm, prickly.
morphology_keys.capsule: Ovoid, about 40–50 × 15–25 mm excluding prickles; prickles very unequal, often branched, with the longest commonly 15–35 mm.
morphology_keys.flowering: Spring through summer; fruiting summer through fall.
best_field_traits: Fresh latex is orange to reddish-orange; A. albiflora subsp. texana is pale/light yellow.
Mature capsule prickles are very unequal, often branched, and extremely long; longest about 15–35 mm.
Sepal horns are about 8–12 mm and prickly.

high_value_traits: white flower despite the species name referring to orange-red latex

look_alikes.distinction: A. albiflora subsp. texana has pale-yellow latex, shorter mostly unarmed sepal horns, and shorter capsule prickles.
